- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 20–40% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome, model often overshoots in next 3–7 days; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–50% for 2–5 days post-spike.
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 10+ days of high sentiment or price), especially in 15–30 day horizon; add 10–20% buffer for mean-reversion phase.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → -0.33 → 0.67), model often fails to adjust; apply “sentiment switch” rule — forecast should align with sentiment direction within 3–5 days of switch.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early days (1–5) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1.5x historical mean for first 5 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
